model: FCFE at cost of equity, managed-care insurer (engine route)

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: forward judgment: post-2026 revenue growth of 4-6% (Medicare-eligible population +3%/yr plus premium yield) corroborated by the 5.3% equity_5yr_cagr; neither the 11% trailing revenue CAGR (share gains as UNH/Aetna shrink footprint, not repeatable) nor the negative EPS/FCFE CAGRs (Stars trough) are a usable forward rate
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (4.9-5.3%) diverges by more than 30% from revenue (10.9-11.8%) and EPS (-17 to -24%). Revenue compounded on MA membership share gains while earnings collapsed on the H5216 Star Ratings loss and industry-wide MA margin compression; FY2025 EPS $9.87 is a trough, not a trend.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the FCFE proxy (net income less 5% of the revenue change), the series this model discounts: FY2020 $2,754m, FY2022 $2,316m, FY2025 $608m. Reported FCF (OCF - capex) CAGRs are shown for reference only: FY2025 reported FCF of $375m is CMS-timing noise, not economics. SBC-adjusted and reported series diverge by less than 0.2pp because SBC is 0.19% of revenue.

scenario_narratives.base: Two-year earnings trough on the H5216 Star Ratings loss, then a partial recovery to a 3.0% consolidated pretax margin by 2030, which is mid-cycle for Humana in a post-V28 world where CMS rates run below cost trend. FY2026 revenue +22% on AEP share gains, decelerating to 5% then 3% as the company prices for margin. The value is almost entirely in years 4-10 and the terminal: the FY2026 revenue jump consumes ~$1.4bn of statutory capital, so near-term FCFE is roughly nil.
scenario_narratives.bull: Management's plan delivered a year or two late: H5216 returns to 4 stars in the Oct-2026 release, restoring the bonus in payment-year 2028; cost trend moderates on value-based care; Humana becomes the largest MA carrier with 7-8% growth through 2028; consolidated pretax reaches 3.8% by 2030 (EPS around management's $38-42 2028 target). Bull needs three independent things to go right (Stars, trend, CMS rates), so it is not over-weighted.
scenario_narratives.bear: H5216 misses 4 stars again, CMS benchmark increases keep lagging a 7-8% cost trend with double-digit drug inflation, RADV and the DOJ FCA case add cost, and Humana sheds membership to reprice. Margin recovers only to 2.0%, growth reverts to demographics. Year-1 FCFE is negative; the business survives comfortably (no solvency question) but earns roughly FY2023-FY2024 economics in perpetuity.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Humana is valued as an equity stream: net income after interest, less the equity retained for statutory capital as MA revenue grows, capitalised at a 9% cost of equity with no net-debt deduction (holding-company debt is charged through interest expense). The valuation deliberately neither extrapolates the FY2026 trough (GAAP EPS at least $6.52) nor adopts management's 2028 EPS target of $38-42; base settles at a 3.0% consolidated pretax margin in 2030, roughly two-thirds of Humana's FY2019-FY2023 average, reflecting structural CMS rate pressure. The scenario spread is wide because the Star Ratings outcome is binary and arrives in the Oct-2026 release; the current price sits near the probability-weighted value, meaning the market is already paying for a partial recovery and offers little margin of safety against the bear path.
key_risks_to_valuation: Oct-2026 Star Ratings release: H5216 failing to return to 4 stars pushes the bonus recovery beyond payment-year 2028 and moves the base toward the bear path (roughly $180/share of value between the two)
Medical and pharmacy cost trend (7-8%, double-digit drug) proving structural rather than transitory, so repricing continually lags cost
CMS 2027-2028 rate notices and V28 risk-model phase-in setting benchmarks below trend industry-wide

Statutory capital retention on the 2026 membership surge (~5% of incremental revenue assumed) is a judgment; a higher RBC requirement or a capital contribution to subsidiaries would reduce distributable earnings further
DOJ False Claims Act broker-payment complaint and RADV audit exposure, which are not reserved in the margin paths
Terminal value is capped at 15x FCFE; the valuation is terminal-heavy because years 1-3 contribute almost no distributable cash

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 163.11-428.88
data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL companyfacts via scripts/build_facts_xbrl.py, FY2006 to Q1 2026, exported to HUM_Metrics.csv; balance sheet and share count from the Q1 2026 10-Q; buybacks and cash taxes from the kpis table
data_sources.qualitative: HUM_Analysis.json (2026-09-29): Q2 2026 earnings guidance (GAAP EPS at least $6.52, adjusted at least $9.00, benefit ratio 92.5-93.0%, cost trend 7-8%, MA pretax margin at least 3% by 2028, 2028 EPS $38-42 reference), Star Ratings history for H5216, CenterWell/MaxHealth and Gentiva transactions, DOJ litigation

inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL cash-flow statement add-back (ShareBasedCompensation), FY2025 10-K. Cash taxes on net-share settlement not separately captured in the XBRL pull; at 0.19% of revenue SBC is immaterial to the valuation and the omission is well inside rounding.
inputs.share_count_basis: Q1 2026 10-Q: 120.65m basic shares outstanding at 31 Mar 2026 plus ~0.35m dilutive awards = 121.0m fully diluted; held FLAT because SBC is expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count). Buybacks are token ($151m FY2025, $107m Q1 2026) while capital is retained for MA growth and margin repair.
inputs.wacc_rationale: The discount rate is a COST OF EQUITY, not a WACC, because the flows are FCFE (post-interest net income less equity retained for statutory capital). USD build: 10y UST ~4.2% + 0.95 beta x 5.0% ERP = ~9.0%. Beta is set above HUM's historical ~0.6 because the earnings stream is now dominated by a single regulator's annual decisions (CMS rate notice, Star Ratings, RADV); the same 9.0% is used in all three scenarios so risk is charged once, in the scenario weights, not twice.
inputs.lease_treatment: None required. Operating leases (CenterWell clinics, offices) are inside GAAP pretax income via rent expense; no lease liability is added to net debt because net debt is held at zero on the FCFE route.
inputs.nci_treatment: No material NCI. FY2025 net income is attributable; the Gentiva minority stake was sold in 2026 (~$900m) and funded the MaxHealth clinic purchase, so neither appears in the bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: FCFE capitalised at cost of equity, run through the owner-FCF engine with net_debt = 0 (same precedent as IAG.AX and GL, which override the dcf-methods default of BVPS-compounding for insurers that do not compound book: HUM equity went $16.1bn FY21 to $17.7bn FY25 with $4.7bn of buybacks in between and ~$10bn of it is goodwill). Why not owner-FCF at WACC: Humana's OCF is swung by CMS prepayment timing (Q3-22 +$8.5bn, Q1-23 +$6.7bn, FY25 only $0.9bn against $1.2bn net income), the $20bn+ investment portfolio backs statutory reserves and cannot be treated as surplus cash, and subsidiary dividends to the parent are capped by RBC rules, so the distributable flow is net income less statutory capital retained. ENGINE MAPPING: ebitda_margin_path = GAAP pretax margin + sbc_pct, so that after the engine deducts SBC the line is GAAP pretax income (already after ~$0.7bn interest expense and including investment income on the reserve portfolio, which is operating float income and NOT stripped; the portfolio is correspondingly not added to the bridge, per the matching-asset rule). da_pct = 0 and capex_pct = 0 because D&A and capex are inside pretax margin; wc_capture_pct = -5 models equity retained for statutory capital at ~5% of incremental revenue (health-insurer RBC target capital ~5-6% of premium; FY19-FY23 retained equity was ~10% of incremental revenue but that included the debt-funded Kindred at Home acquisition). The $14.0bn holding-company debt is charged through interest expense in pretax income, so net_debt is 0 in the bridge; deducting it would double-count. cash_tax_rate 24% = HUM's normal GAAP effective rate (state taxes plus permanent items); no NOL shelter. last_fcf = FY2025 FCFE proxy = net income $1,203m less 5% x $11,903m revenue growth = $608m, NOT reported_fcf - sbc (that figure, $134m, is CMS-timing noise). ANCHORS: FY0 = FY2025 (Dec year-end); year 1 = FY2026, three-quarters elapsed at valuation date; balance sheet and share count from the Q1 2026 10-Q (31 Mar 2026), the latest in the Metrics file. FY2026 revenue is NOT from a guidance paragraph (none extracted): Q1 2026 revenue $39.6bn was +23.5% YoY and Q1 has been a stable 24.8-25.1% of the full year for three years, implying ~$158-159bn; base uses +22%. GUIDANCE USED: FY2026 GAAP EPS at least $6.52 (NI ~$0.79bn, pretax ~0.66% of revenue) and adjusted EPS at least $9.00 (pretax ~0.92%); base year-1 pretax 0.85% sits between the two because both are floors and Q2 beat. The Star Ratings collapse on H5216 (4.5 to 3.5 stars, ~$3.5bn bonus headwind) is a genuine two-year trough: the 2027 payment-year bonus was already set by the Oct-2025 Stars release (~20% of members in 4+ star plans), so recovery cannot arrive before payment-year 2028 and hinges on the Oct-2026 Stars release. Management's 2028 targets (MA pretax margin at least 3%, EPS $38-42) are NOT adopted as base: base reaches 3.0% consolidated pretax in 2030 and holds it, which is mid-cycle for HUM (FY19-FY23 average ~4.4%, but CMS rate-setting below trend and V28 have compressed industry MA margins structurally). Bull adopts the management path (3.8% by 2030); bear assumes H5216 does not recover and CMS rates keep lagging cost trend (2.0% mid-cycle). Street basis (SBC as non-cash) sits ~$45/share above house: SBC is only 0.19% of revenue but the revenue base is $200bn+, so the charge is ~$0.4bn/yr, and at 15x that is ~$5bn of PV. The 15x FCFE cap binds in all three scenarios (Gordon at 9%/3% would be 17x), so the sensitivity grid is flat at discount rates of 8% and below; the cap, not terminal growth, sets the terminal value.
inputs.capital_retention_note: wc_capture_pct = -5: for every $1 of incremental revenue, $0.05 of net income is retained as statutory capital in the regulated subsidiaries and is not distributable. The FY2026 revenue step-up (+$28bn) therefore consumes ~$1.4bn of FY2026 earnings, which is why year-1 FCFE is close to zero or negative in all three scenarios and why buybacks have been token: this is a finding, not a modelling artefact.

bear.ebitda_margin_note: = GAAP pretax margin [0.7, 1.0, 1.5, 1.9, 2.0 ...] + sbc_pct 0.19. H5216 stays at 3.5 stars through the Oct-2026 release, CMS benchmark increases keep lagging 7-8% cost trend (double-digit drug trend, GLP-1s), DOJ FCA litigation adds cost; Humana sheds membership to reprice and settles at 2.0% consolidated pretax, roughly FY2023-FY2024 economics.
bear.narrative: The Stars trough becomes structural: H5216 misses 4 stars again in Oct-2026 (payment-year 2028 bonus lost too), CMS rate notices stay below medical and pharmacy cost trend, RADV audits and the DOJ broker-payment case add cost, and Humana has to shed membership in 2027-2028 to reprice. Consolidated pretax margin recovers only to 2.0%, growth reverts to demographic 3%, terminal growth 2.5%, 13x cap. Year-1 FCFE is negative as the FY2026 revenue step-up consumes statutory capital at a 0.7% margin.

base.ebitda_margin_note: = GAAP pretax margin [0.85, 1.6, 2.5, 2.9, 3.0 ...] + sbc_pct 0.19. FY2026 between the GAAP ($6.52) and adjusted ($9.00) EPS floors; FY2027 modest repricing and cost-ratio gains with the Stars bonus still lost; FY2028 partial H5216 recovery; 3.0% consolidated pretax mid-cycle from 2030 (below management's 2028 target).
base.narrative: FY2026 revenue +22% on the Q1 run-rate (AEP share gains as UNH and Aetna cut MA footprint), then 6%/5%/5% as Humana prices for margin rather than growth, decaying to 3% terminal. Pretax margin troughs at 0.85% in FY2026, 1.6% in FY2027 with the Stars bonus still lost, recovers to 2.5% in FY2028 on a partial H5216 return to 4 stars, and settles at 3.0% consolidated (MA ~3% plus CenterWell), which is mid-cycle for HUM post-V28. Cost of equity 9%, terminal 3%, 15x FCFE cap.

bull.ebitda_margin_note: = GAAP pretax margin [0.95, 2.0, 3.3, 3.7, 3.8 ...] + sbc_pct 0.19. Management's path: H5216 back to 4 stars in the Oct-2026 release, MA pretax margin at least 3% by 2028, EPS in the $38-42 range by 2028 and 3.8% consolidated thereafter (still below the FY19-FY23 average of ~4.4%).
bull.narrative: Stars recover on schedule: H5216 returns to 4 stars in the Oct-2026 release, restoring most of the ~$3.5bn bonus in payment-year 2028; medical cost trend moderates as value-based care (68% of individual MA) delivers the inpatient favourability seen in 2026; Humana becomes the largest MA carrier and keeps 7-8% growth through 2028; CenterWell scales third-party revenue. Consolidated pretax reaches 3.8% by 2030, in line with management's 2028 EPS target of $38-42 delivered a year or two late. Same 9% cost of equity; 16x cap.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: earnings depend on a single regulator (CMS rate notice, Star Ratings, RADV), the recovery thesis rests on an unproven return of H5216 to 4 stars, and the Oct-2026 Stars release is a binary event weeks away. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs Stars, cost trend and CMS rates all to break Humana's way, and the stock has already re-rated from $163 to $390 on the recovery narrative. Base 50%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
